FINAL PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS: 
A. RIGHT BREAST, WIRE-LOCALIZED EXCISION: 
Focal atypical ductal hyperplasia with calcifications. 
Multifocal lobular neoplasia (atypical lobular hyperplasia). 
Multifocal foreign body type giant cell reaction with calcifications. 
Fibrous scar, consistent with remote biopsy site. 
 
Note: There is an unusual multifocal foreign body type giant cell reaction with 
calcifications, concentrated in and around the scar. Some foci are round and 
the size of large ducts, superficially mimicking comedo-type ductal carcinoma 
in-situ (DCIS). The possibility of so-called "vanishing" or "healing" DCIS was 
considered, but ultimately, there is no evidence to support carcinoma. Instead, 
the findings are consistent with an unusual giant cell reaction, likely to blood 
products and fat necrosis, with dystrophic calcifications. Immunohistochemical 
stains for epithelial markers ( REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID  and  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID .3/ REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID .2) do not show evidence of 
epithelial cells in these areas, supporting this interpretation. The resection 
margins of the specimen were inked and microscopically evaluated.

Chief Complaint: This 62-year-old female was referred to the fine needle 
aspiration clinic by Dr. John Muse for consultation and diagnosis of a right 
neck mass. 
 
Clinical History: Right neck mass underlying platysma 
Review of Symptoms: 
Constitutional: None. 
 
Allergy to lidocaine/latex: None. 
Medications/anticoagulants: None. 
 
Social History: Non-contributory. 
 
Family History: Non-contributory. 
 
Past Medical History: Recent breast biopsy diagnosed as ADH. 
 
Review of Patient Data: 
Office Notes: Reviewed. 
 
Physical Examination: Laterality was established according to departmental 
protocol. Examination of the neck revealed a right submandibular soft, mobile 
mass measuring 3.8cm in great dimension using ultrasonogram. 
 
Assessment: Based on the clinical history and physical examination, an FNAB is 
warranted. 
 
Procedure: The procedure and complications were explained to the patient and 
consent was obtained. 2 aspirates were performed using 25 gauge needles without 
anesthesia and without complications. The mass was very soft to the needle with 
almost no resistant. Expression of the aspirate onto the slide revealed liquid 
fat. No slides were stained for immediate evaluation; additional tissue was 
submitted for further evaluation. 
 
Rapid Interpretation: Liquid fat grossly consistent with lipoma. No rapid 
done. 
 
Disposition: The immediate interpretation findings were discussed with the 
patient. The preliminary results were communicated to Dr. John Muse by e-mail.

region of the tubular carcinoma.

atypical ductal hyperplasia present <0.1cm from the superior, inferior, 
anterior, posterior, and lateral margins.

LOW-GRADE B-CELL LYMPHOMA MOST CONSISTENT WITH SPLENIC MARGINAL ZONE LYMPHOMA. 
 
 
NOTE: The resection margins of the specimen were inked and microscopically 
evaluated. 
 
The specimen consists of fibroadipose breast tissue with dense patchy 
infiltrates of small to medium-sized lymphoid cells, occasionally clustered 
around blood vessels. These cells have scant to moderate quantity of pale 
cytoplasm, oval to irregular nuclear contours and coarse chromatin. There are 
small, somewhat irregularly shaped aggregates of larger lymphoid cells with 
moderate cytoplasm, dispersed chromatin and prominent nucleoli, likely 
representing reactive follicle centers. Immunostains reveal the smaller 
lymphoid cells to be  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID + BCL-2+ BCL-6- B cells. The Ki-67 proliferation 
index is 5%. The aggregated larger cells are  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID +  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID + BCL-6+ BCL-2- B cells 
with 80% Ki-67 positivity, consistent with reactive germinal center cells. 
 REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID  highlights irregularly shaped follicular dendritic cell meshworks 
associated with the larger lymphoid cells. Cyclin- REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID  staining is negative, and 
there is weak, patchy IgD staining. In-situ hybridization for kappa and lambda 
immunoglobulin light chains shows an excess of kappa-expressing cells. There 
are scattered  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID + T cells. Flow cytometric analysis (ML-10- REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID ) 
demonstrates a monotypic (kappa+) B-cell population. 
 
In summary, the morphology and immunophenotype are consistent with involvement 
by the patient's previously diagnosed low-grade B-cell lymphoma with slight 
plasmacytic differentiation; in a patient with massive splenomegaly, the 
lymphoma is best-classified as splenic marginal zone lymphoma. See also 
results of cytogenetics (CG-10- REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID ).
